findings.finding: On Windows the package managers are .CMD shims: shutil.which('npm') -> 'C:\Program Files\nodejs\npm.CMD', but CreateProcess does not resolve a bare 'npm', so subprocess.run(['npm','ci']) raises FileNotFoundError. install() catches nothing and ensure() lets it escape, so 'orchflows sync' on this host tracebacks for any trusted item carrying package.json plus a lockfile whenever node is on PATH -- the Goal clause 'runs the lockfile install ... else reports the remedy' does neither. The suite is green because every spawn is injected; no check crosses the one real spawn site.

findings.where: scripts/orchflows_envs.py::prune, called from scripts/orchflows.py::_report_dependencies on both sync forms
findings.finding: prune keeps only the (kind, name) pairs in the inventory resolvable FROM THE VANTAGE sync runs at. Environments live under one machine-wide ~/.orchflows/envs/<kind>/<name>/ whichever ring declared the item, but a project ring's items are in the inventory only when sync runs inside that project. So a plain 'orchflows sync' from the home (or any directory outside a project) deletes every trusted project item's built environment on the machine, and 'sync --project' in project A deletes project B's. The item was not removed from any ring; section 8's trigger is 'an item is removed from the ring -> sync prunes'. Recovery is a rebuild in each project -- which section 8's '2 GB model dependency' row prices, and its 'no network at sync' row turns into a launch refusal for an item that was built an hour earlier.
findings.evidence: R5 in the scratch checkout, module API, no tree mutation: one home + one trusted project ring, project item 'heavy' with requirements.txt and a pre-built env dir under home/envs/skill/heavy. prune(inventory from the project's vantage) -> [] and the env survives; prune(inventory from a vantage outside the project) -> [('skill','heavy')] and the env is gone. The executor's report flags 'Prune is literal' for a different case (an item that dropped its requirements.txt), not this one.
findings.ground: verification.md section 10, second ground. Counter-reading the join may weigh: the Goal's own words are 'items no longer in the inventory', which the code satisfies literally -- under the four grounds the ticket Goal enumerates none fires; under section 10 and the Lens's 'including its failure paths' it is a correctness finding at the fixed identity, and the destroyed state is the launch path's.

findings.finding: run() collapses subprocess.TimeoutExpired and OSError into the same (None, '') so a probe that takes longer than PROBE_TIMEOUT (10 s) reads as "could not run" -- the failure is loud but untyped: a reader cannot tell a missing shim from a slow probe from a wrong command, and the probe's output is never surfaced. Craft: failure is loud AND typed.
findings.evidence: R4 in the scratch checkout: probe 'python -c "import time; time.sleep(30)"' with PROBE_TIMEOUT set to 1.0 -> "probe '...' could not run".

causes.cause: Both spawn sites pass the declared name as argv[0] instead of the executable shutil.which already resolved, and orchflows_node.install lets OSError escape untyped. On POSIX the two are the same string; on Windows the .CMD shims that node's package managers ship as differ, and CreateProcess does not consult PATHEXT.
causes.smallest_change: One helper (orchflows_tools, e.g. executable(name) -> shutil.which(name) or name) applied to argv[0] at the two spawn sites: orchflows_tools.run (covers the probe and the --version read at once) and orchflows_node.install (or ensure passing the which(command[0]) result it already holds as the command's head). In install, catch OSError and raise the existing RuntimeError text so a spawn that cannot start is loud and typed like a non-zero exit. Two checks, one per seam, deterministic on every platform: inject a which that returns a path and a recording runner/installer, and assert the spawned argv[0] is the which result, not the bare name; plus one check that install turns OSError into RuntimeError. Fits the sealed license (U12's own modules).

causes.cause: The orphan test is 'absent from the inventory at this vantage', but an environment is keyed machine-wide by (kind, name) and declared by an item that may be visible only from another vantage.
causes.smallest_change: Decide orphanhood from the environment's own stamp, which orchflows_envs.build already writes with the declaring 'requirements' path: an environment is an orphan when its stamp's requirements file no longer exists on disk (the declaring item is gone), or when it carries no readable stamp AND no inventory record claims it (a half-built tree). Keep every stamped environment whose declaring file still exists, in the inventory or not. One added check: a trusted project item's built environment survives prune from a vantage outside that project; the existing exactly-the-orphan check keeps its reading. Fits the sealed license (orchflows_envs.py, its test module).
